notes.title: Multiplayer Save System Out Now!
notes.content:
Save System!
Hello everyone!
Thank you for your patience while I've been working on this key feature. Multiplayer saving is now available! 

Multiplayer Save-system
The game will auto-save every time you enter the map scene or enter the portal room after a boss (you will see a little wizard icon in the top right when the game is saving). To reconnect to a game, the host clicks "Continue Multiplayer Run" in the main menu, and all players that we're previously in the match reconnect to this lobby via a join-code. You will not be able to start the run until all previous players have connected. If you try to join a run that you were not part of, the system will reject your join attempt. 

Changes

 Multiplayer Save System!
 Added the "Dark Wizard" boss variant for the forest!
 Unique icons for each boss appear on the map in preparation for more boss variants to come...
 Buffed Abomination boss slightly in hardcore mode
 Changed the goblins in hardcore mode slightly

Bug Fixes

 Added a cloud diagnostics service so I can review crash logs when they happen
 Fixed a bug where Barricade for the Viking was costing twice as much mana as it should
 Hardcore achievements for the Forest and Desert should register properly now
 UI fixes for ultrawide resolution
 Fixed a bug where Chorus of Courage for Bard was not working
 Fixed a bug where an armored skeleton was not appearing for clients in hardcore mode in one of the encounters
 Added a fix for a bug where the game got caught in an infinite loop if you died to poison

Coming Next
With working on the multiplayer save system I have all the systems set up to allow players to view each others decks and hands. Exciting! Next up I will be working on viewing your teammates decks and hands, and a Desert boss variant. 

Let me know what you think!
Thanks for reading! If you have any thoughts, comments or concerns please don't hesitate to leave a comment below!

Jamie
FROG Game Studios

notes.title: Save System is Coming!
notes.content:
Thank you
Hi Dungeon Divers,
Thank you to everyone who has been playing over the past launch week and welcome all new players!
Into the Dungeon has surpassed my expectations for launch and with that has come some really important feedback.
Feedback
I've been monitoring feedback on the forums and in reviews and I've taken note of it all. However, two main things have come to my attention:
[olist]
 Into the Dungeon needs a save system
 There needs to be enemy variation from run to run[/olist]

Roadmap
I care about the success and lasting enjoyability of Into the Dungeon so I'm planning to do something about these sore points. 
Save System
Moving forward, along with fixing other bugs, I will be working on implementing a save system for single-player so you can stop mid-way through a run and pick it up later where you left off. It will also auto-save in the case you run into a game crashing bug.

(On the note game crashing bugs, the one where the game crashes upon entering the last boss, I'm really sorry to everyone who has experienced this. I deeply want to get it fixed and will continue to work on the issue for the coming update)

Just to reiterate, I will be implementing a Single-player Save System first. Saving for multiplayer will likely come shortly after the single player system but I foresee it having some added complexity and I want to get a single-player version out ASAP.
Content Update
Following the single-player save system I will release a free content update. The content update will add a  new boss as a variation for the Forest and Desert. With each boss countering a certain playstyle, this will hopefully make each run feel more fresh and exciting.

Let me know what you think!
If you're reading this post and your excited about the changes let me know in the comments! I check these posts frequently and your feedback is what guides my development, so please speak up! Additionally, I've heard mixed feedback on the timer in Hardcore mode. I found it really fun when I was playing with friends, but I can see how it could be frustrating in single-player. What do you think? Do you like the timer, or is a pointless frustration?

Thank you again for your support and I am grateful for your patience as I work to make this game into what you and I both know it can be.

Jamie
FROG Game Studios

notes.title: Build 1.0 Patch Notes!
notes.content:
Into the Dungeon is out in Full Release
Oh my gosh! It's finally happened! Into the Dungeon 1.0 is out and available to play! I am so excited to bring you this update. I've been working hard over the past couple weeks making lots of changes. If you've been playing Into the Dungeon since the beginning or you are just hopping in now, there's lots for everyone to enjoy! 

Price Increase
With all of the new content since the beginning of early access I have raised the price to buy Into the Dungeon to $13.99 USD and $17.99 CAD. I have always planned on increasing the price upon releasing 1.0 and feel these prices more accurately reflect the new value of Into the Dungeon as an experience. 

New stuff 
Visual Update
The Portal room, the Desert, and the Dungeon all have new background art. I am ecstatic with the new look of Into the Dungeon and am excited for all of you to see it. The Desert and Dungeon background as well as the Forest background were all done by the talented artist Karen Xu. 

Hardcore mode
Once you have completed the game on classic mode you will unlock hardcore mode. You can choose this after you select your character and before entering the portal room. Only the host of the game needs to have beaten the game for all players in a lobby to play in hardcore mode, but it is recommended that everyone be familiar with Into the Dungeon before trying it out. 

Hardcore mode offers enemies with increased stats as well as timer. In single-player the timer for your turn is 20 seconds, and for multiplayer it's 30 seconds. The timer adds a fun pressure as you crunch to get all of your actions out before time is up. Discord or some form of voice chat is highly recommended in multiplayer.

Dungeon boss 
No longer are the days of the tiny skeleton at the end of the run. The new mob boss of Into the Dungeon is the Abomination, a hulking bio-mechanical creature piloted by an evil brain in a jar. Lookout for this one, I've heard it takes combat enhancing "juice". 

Choose to begin your journey at any act
I've heard feedback from some players about the struggles of not having a save system. Unfortunately I don't have the resources to re-work the game engine to facilitate saving, but I've added a feature to hopefully alleviate some of the mid-run loss woes. 

Once you complete the prior respective boss, you can start your run at the Desert or the Dungeon with bonus starting gold. This will allow for shorter runs if you want to have a quick play-through with friends, and gives the option to pick-up where you left off if you had to go mid way through a previous run. 

 Changes 
Sand Guardian Rework
I've reworked the Sand Guardian's move set entirely. My goal for all of the bosses was for them to have phases, and I believe I've achieved that with both the Abomination and the Sand Guardian. 

Dynamic Card Text
I noticed while watching friends & family play test Into the Dungeon that the math required by some cards could prove confusing and just generally not fun. I've added text to cards with complex formulas that updates in real time to the values that change during a combat. For example, Spear Wall, an X cost card that attacks X times, will now read "Attack 3 (X) times..." when you have 3 mana. 

Offline mode
You can now play Into the Dungeon without an internet connection!

Additional Changes

You can now hide the scrying overlay to view what enemies are intending to and then re-open it to make your decision.
Added a counter to 3 leaf clover artifact so you now what attack you are at and can plan your damage accordingly. 
Increased the amount of gold in the "Take gold" option after desert combats. 
Reduced the damage the worms do in the Desert in single player.
Added unique battle themes to the Dungeon and Desert boss battles. 
If a card cannot be upgraded, the "Upgrade" button will not appear on the shop pop-up. 
Added indicators on the bosses health bars to signal at what health they will enrage or change phases.

 Bug Fixes

 Rekindle and Set Ablaze should now properly draw cards from your exhaust pile
 Fixed a bug where the bards upgraded cleanse poison card was only healing if the target was poisoned
 Removed "Marching Melody" card from the bard set
 Fixed some audio bugs that were happening in the wolf and Forest boss fights
 Fixed text overflow on enemy HP bars
 Fixed a bug where 4p goblins had the difficulty of 2p goblins
 Fixed a bug where the floating skulls in 4p had their statuses stacking vertically instead of horizontally


I am once again so excited for everyone to get to play the full version of Into the Dungeon. It has been an amazing journey learning and creating this game over the course of the past year. I look forward to a bright future and lots more Into the Dungeon.

Jamie
FROG Studios

notes.title: Full Release
notes.content:
Into the Dungeon will be entering 1.0 on March 22nd 
I am so excited to announce that Into the Dungeon will be leaving Early Access on March 22nd, 2024.
Thank you for all of your support and feedback during the Early Access phase of Into the Dungeon, it has been instrumental to the continued development of this game. In preparation for full release I have been working hard on addressing some long running bugs and making improvements across the board. Some things to look out for in the 1.0 update are:


 QOL upgrade for solo players
 Fixes for long running bugs
 QOL improvements for cards & artifacts
 Hardcore mode
 Tuning of enemies
 Massive visual upgrades
 and more!

After Release
I look forward to seeing all of you playing the full released version of the game. Development will not stop after full release. I will continue to monitor the discord and forums for bugs, and make changes and updates as necessary. 

I'm so grateful to every single person who has purchased Into the Dungeon. You have given me the confidence and resources to pursue a passion of mine and that wouldn't be possible with out the support of this community. From the bottom of my heart, thank you so much.

Jamie
FROG Studios

New Forest Art
The incredible Artist Karen Xu has completed the first of 3 backgrounds for Into the Dungeon. You will surely notice a change in scenery when you enter the Forest now. The Desert and Dungeon Visual Updates are coming soon...

Tutorial
In the Main Menu there is now a "How to Play" button that will take you to a board game like instruction manual on how to play the game. Here you will be coached by the wizard frog Sir Wizzington the Third himself. It's always helpful to know how to play a game before you try and beat it!

Changes
No major changes this week, but a few worth mentioning.

 The giant in the forest deals less damage in singleplayer so you won't get walloped for a third of your hp if you unluckily draw no block cards on his attack.
 The character select screen now offers more information into the play style of each of the classes. Gone are the role tags Tank, Damage, Support. These tags, I believe, were leading people to falsely believe that some classes weren't suited to solo play. All of the classes are extremely capable of making it to the end and defeat the final boss!

Bug Fixes
Due to the excitement of putting the new art in I haven't fixed many bugs this week. However I did get at least one fixed.

 You should now be able to unlock achievements for completing the final boss, and for doing so on each of the classes! Go get that 100%!

notes.title: Update 2: Updated Mobs and Balance Changes!
notes.content:
Update 2 Patch Notes!
Thanks to everyone who has been playing and sharing the game! We hope you have enjoyed playing so far as we roll out our first weekly update.

Balance Changes
We had noticed that players weren't making it very far on their first play through, or contrastingly, they were wiping the entire game with a simple build. We shadow-pushed a hotfix to the forest enemies earlier this week. In this update we go further to address both of these issues.
Enemy AI and Changes
We have changed the enemy AI from choosing random abilities from a list to being given a set of abilities they do on rotation. This change gives us greater control over each encounter and therefore results in a more tailored and fun experience. 
The Forest encounters have been completely reworked, with some enemies getting an entirely new move set. The only encounters that have gone largely unchanged in the forest are the fairies and the fancy goblin. 
We've also added new art for the intention icons that appear above enemies heads. This rollout isn't entirely complete with this update but will be fully implemented by next Friday.
Card Changes

 Returning Shield is getting nerfed from 5(7) block down to 3(4).
 Masochism now applies 2(3) exposed to the player up from 1(2).
 Divine Strikes is now Exhaust.
 Blaze now costs 1 mana, up from 0.
 Scalding Sorcery no longer has a minimum of 1 mana cost, but instead the cost resets when played.
 Exhaustive Power now reduces cost by 2(3) and the upgrade now costs 1 mana instead of 0.
 Glance is now 4(6) damage down from 6(8) and is Exhaust
 Viking and Paladin starter card upgrade values are now in line with the other classes.
 Blind Aggression damage is reduced down to 3(4).
 Enormous Parry is now exhaust.
 Poke now does 2(4) damage.
 Random Attacks now gives 2(3) attacks instead of 3.

General Changes

 Start with 150g up from 50g

Bug Fixes

 Returning Shield should always return when it is supposed to now.
 Fixed room numbers resetting when exiting to main menu and starting a new run.
 Fixed grammatical errors and typos within the cards.
 Volume settings now save in-between games.
 Fixed bug where Pyroblast+ was unplayable.
 Fixed a bug where poison was ticking after players died.
 Increased scroll speed when viewing deck in combat.
 Poison stacks are now tracked within Incoming Damage.
 Fixed a bug where venom stacks would go down to 2 even with Coated Weapons active.
 Fixed a bug where Plague+ wasn't working.
 Fixed a bug where Daze cards from enemies were being added twice to the discard pile, causing a lot of other issue (such as augury not reducing in cost when it should).

Next Week
In our following update we will continue updating all of the enemies in the game and introducing some new encounters. Additionally, we will be adding some new cards and artifacts in to the game!

Thanks for reading!
Jamie
Lead Developer
FROG Game Studios

notes.title: Early Access Release Date
notes.content:
https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/44359729/319d85fc98db1f07c96d7c5ed08fa3fa4316fb64.png
Early Access
Into the Dungeon will be released on Friday, October 20th, 2023 at 10:00 am! We are so excited to be releasing our first game to steam. This title has been underway for nearly 8 months and it feels great to be getting it into the hands of players. 

Update Schedule
We plan to push consistent updates to the game every 2 weeks, and balance changes and card tweaks every week. You can plan to expect these updates on Fridays at 10am every week, barring any major holidays.
We have been working hard to iron out as many of the bugs as we can before this release, but please keep in mind that we are a team of 1 developer/artist/composer and 1 game designer. If you do encounter bugs when playing Into the Dungeon Early Access please reach out to us on our discord and we will do our best to tackle them by our bi-weekly updates. 

What about Full Release?
Great question! As excited as we are about entering Early Access, we want to be in full release no later than February of 2024. That's roughly 16 weeks from now.

What are we going to be working on?
We have a busy schedule ahead of us. Here is a list of all the things we will be working on in the next 16 weeks. These items are roughly in the order that we will be working on them, but some items might change or move around so don't treat this too biblically. Some items might have additional "Hope to Have" items that we will add if we have time. 

Enemy Overhaul: Update the enemies in every level to have a more deterministic experience (create repeating patterns in enemies). This also includes introducing more enemy variety and having a major boss at the end of each level. 
-Hope to Have Two boss variants for each level
Music & SFX Overhaul: Create a soundtrack for each section of the game and introduce SFX for every component of the game.
Environment Art Overhaul: Completely update the background art for each level.
-Hope to Have lighting changes throughout the map.
Loot & Rest Scene Update: update the loot and rest scene with art, sfx, and atmosphere.
Final Boss: The addition of a final boss after the last level to really test your final deck.
(Hope to Have) Mystery Scenes: Add mystery scenes to the map that contain meaningful choices that augment your run.
Ability VFX: Complete the implementation of ability FX. (Such as fire raining down when casting Firestorm)
Unlockable Cards: We will add additional cards for each class, as well as a set of cards that allows for a different combo set unlocked upon beating the game.
Tutorial: A tutorial for players new to the roguelike deckbuilding genre that shows them the ropes so they can hop in and start playing as quick as possible.

Conclusion
That's it from me this week. Once again we are so excited to be releasing our first game and we hope you enjoy it. If you ever want to reach out and talk to me or another dev please feel free to join our discord and introduce yourself. Thank you for reading and we hope you enjoy!

Cheers,
Jamie
Lead Developer
Frog GameStudios

notes.title: Devlog 1
notes.content:
-New Cards!-
https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44359729/7a371d085204ca555abf12598f7d7e21c80a4dc7.gif
Over the past couple of weeks we have been crafting and implementing the Paladin class. We wanted to create cards that would make playing the tank fun. We have shield slams, cards that combo with what's in your deck and a class unique buff called "Smite". We're really happy with how it's turned out and we are even taking what we've learned with the Paladin and applying it to the Wizard and the Viking. 

-Progression-
https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44359729/6b8a90834a83b184e8d17151b774c8c59ce09960.gif
In addition to the updates to the Paladin, we also worked on improving our game feel. We've added more feedback on how you are progressing through the game and a statistics popup you can use to check your damage dealt, damage blocked, damage received and gold earned (so you can flex on your friends of course).
Unlockables
I also think it's worth mentioning that we plan to have a set of unlockable cards for each class upon completing a run. In addition to this, we have a Hardcore mode that will become available to players upon completing a run in Classic mode.  

As always we are very excited to get the game in to the hands of players as soon as possible, and we are trying for a big push to get the game out by mid October. 

Thanks for reading,

Jamie

Hello!
My name is Jamie and I am the lead developer on Into the Dungeon. We have been working hard to get the game ready for release in the coming months and I wanted to share with you where we are at, and where we are going. Our design goals have been to design the classes to feel unique but synergistic with one another. Additionally, we are working to make the encounters to feel unique and challenging, but still possible to overcome with strategic play despite the build path you choose to go. 

https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44359729/0dafcc0f80c361f5f0b7cecbbdde04edf0fbb650.gif
What's in the game so far?
The game is already in a playable state with 2 implemented classes each with 30+ unique cards not including card upgrades, 20+ artifacts that modify and enhance specific builds, and the first world of three with elites, standard battles and boss encounters. 

https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44359729/0dc8e37cd453dfd9db0f9837312e3c8e9b06761e.gif
What's to come?
The next couple months are going to be filled with lots of new cards coming into the game and lots of testing. Here is what we are going to be building:

The Paladin and Bard classes along with their unique artifacts,
Unlockable cards for each class (these will be unlocked by beating the game on specific classes)
The next 2 worlds with their own unique encounters,
Random map events, such as upgrades and curses,
Steam achievements,
and finally, Bug fixes and polish!
 
Thanks for reading!
If you want to learn more about what's to come in Into the Dungeon come join our Discord. The rest of the team and I would love to hear from you. Yes, you!

Until next time.

Jamie,
